results.title: How to rollback a broken deployment quickly
results.snippet:
You need at least one previous successful deploy to return to. Instant rollbacks also depend on how many builds Render retains for your workspace plan, as shown below.

|  |  |
---|
| Free web services | Two most recent previous deploys |
| Hobby | 5 |
| Pro | 15 |
| Scale | 30 |
| Enterprise | 30 |

See Render pricing for plan details. If your target is older than your retention window, use a specific commit instead.

Documentation checked: Render between 2026-09-11 and 2026-11-20. [...] - Roll back first and debug second. Restoring service gives you time to investigate. Once you're stable, tools like Jules by Google Labs can help you debug a failed Render deploy.
- Choose a plan whose build retention covers how far back you might need to go.
- Put expand and contract steps in separate deploys.
- Don't ship a migration and a destructive cleanup in the same deploy.
- Don't treat a passing health check as proof that the deploy is correct. [...] In maintenance mode, your web service keeps running but is unreachable from the public internet. Render responds to every incoming request with `503 Service Unavailable` and your maintenance page. You can still reach the service over your private network and through SSH, so you can repair it while users are blocked. Maintenance mode is available only for paid web services.
